Federal authorities have indicted five people tied to a high-tech car theft ring stretching from San Antonio to the border, while two suspects remain at large, according to KGNS. Laredo police warned on October 29 about the methods thieves are using to steal push-to-start vehicles without breaking glass or triggering alarms.

Surveillance video shared by the Laredo Police Department shows suspects approaching targeted vehicles carrying handheld programming equipment. Instead of forcing entry, the thieves access the vehicle's computer system, program and pair a blank key fob on the spot, and take full control of the vehicle. Laredo Police Lt. Charlie Rosales said the thieves can drive the vehicle away within about a minute, and that some stolen vehicles are never recovered.

Investigators say the stolen vehicles are quickly moved to the border and handed over to Mexican cartels. With holiday shopping increasing in major hubs such as San Antonio and Austin, officials warn that push-to-start systems have grown increasingly vulnerable. Despite high-tech crews operating across South Texas, police noted that auto thefts in Laredo have decreased 34 percent year over year.

Authorities advise drivers that relying solely on key fobs or factory alarm locks is no longer enough. Investigators recommend using physical steering wheel locks, parking in well-lit areas under store surveillance cameras, and immediately contacting police if anyone is seen lingering near vehicles with handheld electronics.

Sources:

  • KGNS, "Police warn drivers of high-tech thefts targeting push-to-start vehicles," October 30, 2026

title: Laredo police warn of high-tech thefts targeting push-to-start vehicles
